clue.text: Crowd round in a crypt for Little Boy, maybe

indicators.note: in says the turned-round crowd sits within the words 'a crypt'

parts.note: a crypt is a burial vault, a tomb

indicators.note: round says the word for a crowd is turned about

parts.note: a crowd is a mob

explanation.surface: A throng gathers in a church vault, perhaps for a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Boy' looks like a child, but it was the code name of the bomb dropped on Hiroshima in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Boy was a specific nuclear weapon, so it is an example of the device, signalled by 'maybe'.

clue.text: Volunteers vicar to cut sileage crop

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
REV, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
to etch is to cut lines into a surface

explanation.surface: Volunteers send a clergyman to mow a fodder crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sileage' is an old spelling of silage, fermented cattle fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Tare vetch is a leguminous plant grown as fodder and ensiled for livestock.

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
issue means offspring, here a son

explanation.surface: A tenant's university qualification becomes a point of dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodger' looks like a tenant, but it means a member of a Masonic lodge; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in lodges, so a member of one can be playfully called a lodger.

indicators.note: solved suggests a puzzle worked out, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scotsman cracks the most baffling picture puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means hidden or puzzling in sense, and the superlative of obscure means hardest to understand.

parts.note: basil is a herb

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of the word farm, its middle letters

explanation.surface: A herb farm basically relies on backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Basilar is an anatomical adjective meaning relating to a base, so it concerns what supports something.

clue.text: Idiot Trump initiative world leaders can reverse

indicators.note: reverse says the whole string so far is read backwards
leaders points to the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: World leaders could undo a scheme pushed by Trump, the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials TIW plus TIN make TIWTIN, which 'reverse' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly, foolish person, a straightforward synonym for a dimwit.

clue.text: Far from carrying weight, retired with honour

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the result is read backwards
carrying says the far-off word holds the weight inside it

parts.note: yon is an old word for distant, over there
LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone who once bore no burden withdrew honourably.
explanation.walkthrough: YON 'carrying' LB is YLBON; 'retired' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To act nobly is to behave honourably, with dignity and high principle.

parts.note: a turbo, a turbine-driven charger, is something that drives a motor harder
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: A train driver is given some backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engine driver' reads as a railwayman, but the definition is just 'Engine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop is a jet turbine engine that drives a propeller, as on many small airliners.

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: Someone crosses an island at a fast pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb of travel but is the adjective angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cross means being angry, which is what irate says.

indicators.note: extremely points to the two end letters of the word clear

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: A river in plain trouble presents an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of acute danger or difficulty needing urgent action.

parts.note: a Spaniard is an Iberian, from the Iberian peninsula

explanation.surface: A short Spanish man might have a gruff voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' looks like a hoarse voice, but it is the sled dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siberian husky is a breed of sled dog, so a Siberian dog may be a husky.

clue.text: In the end flat, count out of turn

parts.note: flat means level or even

indicators.note: out of places the count on the outside of the turn

parts.note: a tally is a count
U stands for a turn, as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: Finally the flat is levelled, and somebody counts at the wrong moment.
explanation.walkthrough: U stands for a turn because a U-turn reverses direction; 'out of' puts the count on the outside of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means finally, after some time, which is what in the end means.

clue.text: Unintentionally discover where GI's were reported to be

indicators.note: reported says the words are as they sound when spoken

parts.note: American GIs in wartime Britain were famously 'overpaid

explanation.surface: Stumbling on where American soldiers were said to be stationed.
explanation.walkthrough: The wartime British gibe called GIs 'overpaid, oversexed and over here'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhear is to catch words by chance that were not meant for you.

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone tweaks part of a trade agreement in a dishonest way.
explanation.walkthrough: GATT was the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.
explanation.definitionFit: To attune something is to bring it into harmony, adjusting it to fit.

indicators.note: mistake suggests something gone wrong, so the letters that follow are scrambled

explanation.surface: A lone error made during a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Single describes someone with no spouse, the plain sense of not wed.

clue.text: Roman Catholic bread broken for population all over Christmas

indicators.note: broken bread is torn apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Catholic communion bread is broken for everyone at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas' is Christmas Island in the Indian Ocean, not the festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Millions of these crustaceans live across Christmas Island and swarm over it in their annual migration.

clue.text: Pull just holding head of fragile insect

parts.note: to drag is to pull

indicators.note: holding says the word for just takes a letter inside it

parts.note: just means only

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the word fragile

explanation.surface: Simply tugging something fragile-headed, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonfly is a large winged insect with a long slender body that hunts near water.

clue.text: Lizard and grouse raised in city

parts.note: an anole is a small American lizard
to grouse is to complain, to crab

explanation.surface: A lizard and a game bird are reared in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the bird, but it is the verb to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is a major Spanish port city, the capital of Catalonia.

indicators.note: Fawlty sounds like faulty, so the letters before it are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Mrs Fawlty's pet hate, Sybil from the sitcom.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a British sitcom about a hotel run by Basil and Sybil Fawlty.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small rodent commonly kept in a cage as a household pet.

clue.text: Violent mob in city short cut

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian city

indicators.note: cut says the word for short loses its final letter

parts.note: terse means short or curt

explanation.surface: A violent crowd in a city takes a shortcut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short cut' looks like a route, but 'short' is TERSE and 'cut' docks its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioters are people taking part in a riot, together forming a violent crowd.

indicators.note: pursues says the rage comes after the poisoner

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
ire means rage

explanation.surface: One hopes fury chases a murderer with poison.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim at or long for something, much as to hope for it.

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Choose something from crime fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Select as an adjective means chosen as the best, exclusive, like a top group.

parts.note: 17 is a Spanish city, and in Spanish counting begins with one, two, three

explanation.surface: A nobleman of the city at 17 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman's title, but it means counting, done in Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish for one, two, three is how someone in that city would begin to count.

indicators.note: mistake signals that these letters have gone wrong and need reordering

explanation.surface: Someone strips the bed, regretting an error.
explanation.walkthrough: On a ship, sheets are ropes controlling sails, not bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a vessel is to strip it of rigging, which includes the ropes called sheets.

indicators.note: for starters points to the opening letter of the word thieves

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Thieves begin by stealing a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like money but is the verb to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to beat or pulse heavily, as a heart can pound.

clue.text: Spooner's hunting assistant escaped delicate work

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: a gillie is a Scottish attendant on a hunting or fishing trip
escaped means free

explanation.surface: A hunting guide got away from some fine craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Filigree is ornamental work of fine twisted metal wire, notably delicate.

clue.text: A good way scrap may produce litter

parts.note: a good way off means far
a scrap is a quarrel, a row

explanation.surface: A sensible method for scrap paper might lead to rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish, but it is a brood of young pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrow is a litter of piglets born to a sow.

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
to dog is to follow closely

explanation.surface: Salt served with a main course to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' and 'main' suggest a meal; an old salt is a veteran sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt and sea dog are both informal terms for an experienced sailor.

clue.text: Old sound back in Irishman's pulse

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the Irish name

parts.note: Sean is an Irish man's name

indicators.note: back says the word for the inlet is read backwards

parts.note: a sound is an inlet of the sea, like a bay

explanation.surface: An Irishman's heartbeat has an old ring to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat, but here it is an edible legume seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, and the soya bean is one of them.
